subject.title: [Feature] Decouple dreaming from memory-core — allow any memory plugin to implement dreaming protocol

question: Should OpenClaw add a public memory-plugin dreaming protocol where core manages scheduling/phase orchestration, or should Dreaming remain owned by individual memory plugins and ClawHub packages?
rationale: The requested fix would add durable plugin-SDK/config/runtime surface and may overlap with the open memory role-slot architecture, so automation should not choose the product boundary.

options.title: Coordinate a core protocol
options.body: Use this issue as the canonical design tracker for a narrow dreaming provider contract, coordinated with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88504 before implementation.

options.title: Keep orchestration plugin-owned
options.body: Document that memory plugins may implement their own dreaming pipelines and point users to ClawHub packages like memory-lancedb-dreaming instead of adding a core protocol.

options.title: Defer behind role slots
options.body: Leave this open until the role-slot PR lands or is rejected, then revisit whether memory.dreaming needs a separate provider interface.

recommendation.title: Coordinate a core protocol
recommendation.body: Use this issue as the canonical design tracker for a narrow dreaming provider contract, coordinated with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88504 before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice defines public OpenClaw plugin/config direction and crosses memory, plugin SDK, and ClawHub boundaries.
